title: A feature screenshot is a recipe in the History and a result with counts: read the recipe, then test the result against the volume and topology the recipe must give
summary: Each figure shows the History of a shape built from profiles or primitives plus one feature node (extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, fillet, chamfer, shell), and the resulting body. Every feature has a closed-form volume or topology rule, so the mesh counts and, in the toolbar run, the printed volume and area can be checked by arithmetic.

read_the_figure.question: Does the result have the shape, volume and topology that the feature named in the History should produce from those inputs?
read_the_figure.axes: No data axes. Left: the History, with dependency rows (dep0, dep1) or a single profile row, and the feature as target. Centre: a 3D view with a labelled ground grid (here from about -5 to 2.5) and a scale bar (500 micrometres for the loft). Bottom: the MESH line. In the toolbar runs the lower panel also gives volume, area and a watertightness statement.
look_at: The History: which profiles or primitives feed the feature, and which feature is the target. For loft the two dependencies are the sections it blends, here a circle and a rectangle.

The body. A loft shows a smooth transition between two different sections; an extrude is a straight prism; a revolve of a circle about an axis through it is a ball; a sweep along a path is a tube that bends; a shell of a ball looks like a ball from outside.
The grid labels and scale bar, to compare sizes between runs.
The MESH line and the identity 2V minus F equal to 2 chi. A shell adds an inner surface, so it reads 8 instead of 4.

Toolbar run: the status area prints volume, area, whether the mesh is closed, and a tally of how many nodes are exact, conditionally exact, disclosed approximate or unknown. Read these as the tool's own bookkeeping.
Whether the shape is shown from outside only. Shell and cavity effects are invisible from there.
read_the_figure.proves: That the feature node evaluates on its inputs and gives a closed body of the expected type. With printed volume and area, it also lets you test the result against the formula for that feature. It does not give the dimensions of the inputs.
if_wrong: A revolve whose 2V minus F is 0 when you expected a ball: the profile was offset from the axis and produced a ring.
A shell whose counts show a single surface: the wall thickness is zero or the inner surface was not generated.
A fillet or chamfer screenshot that looks like the unmodified solid: the radius is smaller than the mesh spacing.
A sweep whose tube pinches or self-intersects at a bend: the section radius is larger than the radius of curvature of the path.
A volume and area pair that violates the isoperimetric inequality: one of them is wrong.
must_check: The inputs' dimensions are printed or the profile and path are shown separately.
Each feature's parameter (height, angle, radius, thickness) is stated. None is in these windows.
The status area's volume and area carry units. They are printed without units here.
A section view whenever the feature creates something hidden (shell, cavity).
Resolution is stated (the Resolution box reads 32) and its effect on volume is known.
as_drawn: Read from the status line of the screenshots I opened at full size, exact digits.
loft (circle then rectangle): 5160 vertices, 10316 faces, scale bar 500 micrometres, chi is 2.
shell (sphere input): 6264 vertices, 12520 faces, scale bar 500 micrometres. 2V minus F is 8, chi is 4: two closed surfaces, consistent with a hollow ball seen as a plain disc from outside.
revolve (circle2d input): 4152 vertices, 8300 faces, chi is 2: a ball-like surface, not a ring.

fillet (sphere and box inputs): 3744 vertices, 7484 faces, chi is 2. It has the same counts and the same outline as the smooth union screenshot in the booleans group, so the two cannot be told apart from this view.
sweep along path: 3688 vertices, 7372 faces, scale bar 500 micrometres, chi is 2: a bent tube.

toolbar extrude (a 16-node History): 4928 vertices, 9852 faces, volume 1.99324, area 9.72317, 'closed mesh -- watertight', exactness tally 13 exact, 3 disclosed approximate, 0 unknown. No units are printed.
Not opened at full size: chamfer, sweep circular and the other toolbar versions.

terms.meaning: A 2D shape (circle, rectangle, polygon) that a feature turns into a solid.
Pushing a profile straight along its normal by a height h. The volume is area times height.
Spinning a profile about an axis. By Pappus, the volume is the area times the distance travelled by the centroid.
Moving a section along a path. The section is kept oriented by a frame along the curve.
A smooth body that interpolates between two or more sections.
Rounding or bevelling an edge. A fillet replaces the edge by a circular arc of radius r, a chamfer by a straight cut of leg c.
Hollowing a solid so that only a wall of thickness t remains.
A mesh with no boundary edges: every edge is shared by exactly two triangles.

remember: Extrude volume is area times height; revolve volume is area times the path of the centroid (Pappus).
A fillet of radius r at a right-angle corner removes r squared times (1 minus pi over 4) of area per unit length; a chamfer with equal legs removes r squared over 2.
A shell adds an inner surface: chi goes from 2 to 4 for a ball.
Volume and area of any body satisfy A cubed at least 36 pi V squared.
The feature's parameter is not in the screenshot, so never quote it.

understand.title: Recipe and result
understand.text: The History is a recipe: inputs, then one operation. A feature explains the result only if its parameters are known, so the figure's evidence is the type of the result (topology, closedness) more than its size.

understand.title: Why the status area matters
understand.text: In the toolbar run, volume, area and the watertight statement are numbers you can verify. They turn a picture into a testable claim.

steps.title: Extrude
steps.note: A is the profile area and P its perimeter. The side wall has area P times h and there are two caps.

steps.title: Revolve: Pappus's theorem
steps.note: The centroid of the profile travels a circle of radius equal to its distance from the axis. A circle on the axis gives a ball (chi = 2); a circle off the axis gives a ring (chi = 0).

steps.title: Revolving a semicircle gives a ball
steps.note: Pappus again with a half-disc: area pi R squared over 2, centroid 4R over 3 pi from the axis.

steps.title: Sweep: volume of a tube along a path
steps.tex: V\approx A\,L\quad\text{(section radius smaller than the radius of curvature)}
steps.note: A is the area of the section and L the length of the path. Bishop's rotation-minimising frame keeps the section from twisting. The condition on curvature prevents the tube from folding over itself.

steps.title: Loft: blend two sections
steps.note: The simplest loft: linear interpolation between two sections that share a parameter s. The result depends on how the two sections are matched.

steps.title: Fillet versus chamfer at a right-angle corner
steps.note: A fillet removes the corner square minus a quarter disc. With c = r, the chamfer removes more material: 0.5 r squared against 0.215 r squared.

steps.title: Shell by an absolute-value trick
steps.note: Zero where d = 0 and where d = minus t, negative between them. So the wall is the layer of thickness t below the original surface.

steps.title: Volume and topology of a spherical shell
steps.note: The shell screenshot reads 2(6264) minus 12520, which is 8. Checked by computation. Compare 4 for a solid ball.

steps.title: A sanity test on printed volume and area
steps.note: The isoperimetric inequality: a ball has the least area for a given volume. For the toolbar extrude, A cubed is about 919.2 and 36 pi V squared is about 449.3, so the pair is consistent. Computed from the printed values.

worked.title: How much material does a shell remove, and what does the counting identity say?
worked.problem: The window prints no radius, so take illustrative values R = 1 and t = 0.1. (a) What is the volume of the shell? (b) A shell mesh has 6264 vertices. How many triangles does it have if it is one outer plus one inner closed surface?
worked.answer: (a) about 1.135 cubic units, 27 percent of the solid ball's 4.189. (b) 12520 triangles, which is the number printed in the screenshot.

analyze.q: The shell screenshot looks identical from outside to a plain ball. Which two numbers in the window distinguish them, and how?
analyze.hint: 2V minus F and the vertex count against a solid sphere.

analyze.q: The fillet and smooth union screenshots from different groups have identical mesh counts and outlines. Does that mean fillet and smooth union are the same operation?
analyze.hint: Same inputs, same blend, or same view?

analyze.q: For the revolve screenshot, chi equals 2. What does that say about where the circle sat relative to the axis?

evaluate.q: The toolbar run prints volume and area without units. Is that adequate? Which of the printed numbers would you publish?
evaluate.hint: The checks that do not need units, such as the isoperimetric inequality.

evaluate.q: Is a single outside view adequate for shell, fillet and chamfer screenshots? What would be better?
evaluate.hint: A cut plane through the feature.

create: Design a feature screenshot template: inputs with dimensions, the parameter list, the formula for the expected volume, the printed volume and the relative error.
Write a test that builds a shell of a sphere at three resolutions and verifies that the volume converges to the formula.

checks.q: Why does a shell of a ball have Euler characteristic 4?
checks.hint: How many closed surfaces does it have?
checks.answer: It has two closed ball-like surfaces, an outer one and an inner one, and chi adds: 2 + 2.

checks.q: A profile of area 2 is extruded by 3. What is the volume?
What is the area removed by a fillet of radius 0.5 at a right-angle corner?
A revolve of a circle gives 2V - F = 0. What can you say about the circle and the axis?
checks.answer: The mesh is ring-like (a torus), so the circle did not touch the axis; if it were centred on it the result would be a ball with 2V - F = 4.

checks.q: The toolbar extrude prints volume 1.99324 and area 9.72317. Is the pair plausible?
checks.answer: Yes: A cubed is about 919, which exceeds 36 pi V squared, about 449. It does not prove them right, only that they are possible together.

checks.q: How would you design a fillet test that a plain outside view cannot pass by accident?
checks.hint: A quantity the unfilleted body does not have.
checks.answer: Use a body whose filleted volume is known in closed form, compare the printed volume with it, and add a cut view of the corner.
